title: Rabbi Yochanan ben Dehavai (a Tanna of a Baraita)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rabbi Yehudah ben Teima, as in Sanhedrin 4b, where he said in his name that one blind in one eye is exempt from appearing [at the Temple]. The statement is cited in Chagigah 2a and Arakhin 2b, and there it is Rabbi Yehudah without further designation, but Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Yehudah ben Teima. In Menachot 42b he disagrees with Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel concerning tekhelet.

An aggadic saying of his remains to us in Nedarim 20a, where he said: “The ministering angels told me four things: why are there lame people,” etc. In Avot deRabbi Natan, end of chapter 27, he says: “Whoever says that the halakhah was not created (or: is not fitting) has no share in the world to come.” He said there: “Do not distance yourself from a measure that has no limit, nor from a labor that has no end,” and he told a fine parable about this.

notes.text: The alternative נראית is rendered fitting, not given; saved Vilna Avot deRabbi Natan27 has נבראת. These are alternative readings recorded by Hyman, not a new emendation of the source.
